title: A QR Scan and a Fingerprint Unlock 30 Minutes of YouTube | vitalii.no
description:
On October 14th, YouTube ran uninterrupted for about 80 minutes in my house with zero chores done that day — right after plain TV had already been unlocked that morning by one of the boys' own PIN. The family screen-time gate used to default to open whenever no gated child had started the day, which meant a quiet morning with nobody earning anything was treated exactly like a morning everyone had earned it.

I flipped that default: the gate now needs proof that someone actually finished their tasks, or a live parent override, and reports "nobody" instead of silently granting access. On top of that I built a parent QR pass. The kiosk shows a one-time QR code, the parent's phone scans it, signs in with the Google account already tied to their email, and then confirms with a WebAuthn check — the phone's own fingerprint, face, or screen lock, with no shared password and no separate app to install.

A successful check now buys exactly 30 minutes of access, visible as a live countdown on the TV that turns red in its last 5 minutes, and a parent can cancel it at any time.
